connectionSpecification.description: Reads tables and views of a MySQL database: full refresh, incremental by a cursor column, or CDC from the binlog.

replication_method.description: How rows are read: by SELECT queries (full refresh, or incremental by a cursor column), or as changes from the binlog.

oneOf.description: Reads rows with SELECT queries; incremental streams read the rows whose cursor column is at least the saved value.
oneOf.title: Scan Changes with User Defined Cursor

oneOf.description: Reads a snapshot of each table, then inserts, updates and deletes from the binlog. Needs log_bin=ON, binlog_format=ROW, binlog_row_image=FULL and the REPLICATION CLIENT and REPLICATION SLAVE privileges.

checkpoint_seconds.description: How often the binlog position is saved while the binlog is read.
checkpoint_seconds.title: Checkpoint Interval in Seconds

initial_waiting_seconds.description: Accepted for compatibility with Airbyte's configuration; the binlog is read until the sync is stopped.
initial_waiting_seconds.title: Initial Waiting Time in Seconds

server_id.description: A numeric ID for this replication client, unique among the server's replicas and binlog readers (1-4294967295). When empty, a random ID from 5400-6399 is used.
server_id.title: Server ID

oneOf.title: Read Changes using Binary Log (CDC)

replication_method.title: Update Method

ssl_mode.description: How the connection is encrypted and which server certificates are trusted.

oneOf.description: Connects with encryption when the server supports it, without otherwise.
oneOf.title: preferred

oneOf.description: Always encrypts; the server certificate is not verified.
oneOf.title: required

oneOf.description: Always encrypts and verifies that the server certificate is signed by the given CA.

ca_certificate.description: PEM certificate of the CA that signed the server certificate.
ca_certificate.title: CA certificate

client_certificate.description: PEM client certificate, when the server asks for one.
client_certificate.title: Client certificate

client_key.description: PEM private key of the client certificate.
client_key.title: Client key

oneOf.title: verify_ca

oneOf.description: Always encrypts and verifies the server certificate's CA and that it names the host.

ca_certificate.description: PEM certificate of the CA that signed the server certificate.
ca_certificate.title: CA certificate

client_certificate.description: PEM client certificate, when the server asks for one.
client_certificate.title: Client certificate

client_key.description: PEM private key of the client certificate.
client_key.title: Client key

oneOf.title: verify_identity

ssl_mode.title: SSL Modes

schema_patterns.description: Accepted for compatibility; only the configured database is read.
schema_patterns.title: Schema Patterns

table_patterns.description: SQL LIKE patterns of the tables to list (e.g. ["users%", "orders%"]). Empty lists every table.
table_patterns.title: Table Patterns

tunnel_method.description: Whether to initiate an SSH tunnel before connecting to the database, and if so, which kind of authentication to use.
No ssh tunnel needed to connect to database

ssh_key.description: OS-level user account ssh key credentials in PEM or OpenSSH format (RSA, ECDSA or Ed25519)
ssh_key.title: SSH Private Key

tunnel_host.description: Hostname of the jump server host that allows inbound ssh tunnel.
tunnel_host.title: SSH Tunnel Jump Server Host

tunnel_host_key.description: Public host keys of the jump server, one per line, each in authorized_keys format ("ssh-ed25519 AAAA...") or as a known_hosts line ("bastion.example.com ssh-ed25519 AAAA..."); the whole output of ssh-keyscan works. The tunnel is refused when the server presents none of them. When empty, the host key is not verified.
tunnel_host_key.title: SSH Host Key

tunnel_method.description: Connect through a jump server tunnel host using username and ssh key

tunnel_port.description: Port on the proxy/jump server that accepts inbound ssh connections.
tunnel_port.title: SSH Connection Port

tunnel_user.description: OS-level username for logging into the jump server host.
tunnel_user.title: SSH Login Username

tunnel_host.description: Hostname of the jump server host that allows inbound ssh tunnel.
tunnel_host.title: SSH Tunnel Jump Server Host

tunnel_host_key.description: Public host keys of the jump server, one per line, each in authorized_keys format ("ssh-ed25519 AAAA...") or as a known_hosts line ("bastion.example.com ssh-ed25519 AAAA..."); the whole output of ssh-keyscan works. The tunnel is refused when the server presents none of them. When empty, the host key is not verified.
tunnel_host_key.title: SSH Host Key

tunnel_method.description: Connect through a jump server tunnel host using username and password authentication

tunnel_port.description: Port on the proxy/jump server that accepts inbound ssh connections.
tunnel_port.title: SSH Connection Port

tunnel_user.description: OS-level username for logging into the jump server host.
tunnel_user.title: SSH Login Username

tunnel_user_password.description: OS-level password for logging into the jump server host
tunnel_user_password.title: Password

tunnel_method.title: SSH Tunnel Method

zero_date_handling.description: What a DATE, DATETIME or TIMESTAMP whose month or day is zero (0000-00-00, 2024-00-15) reads as: null reads it as null, fail stops the sync with an error naming the stream, column and row.
zero_date_handling.title: Zero Dates
